object.description: Single-cell RNA-seq preprocessing quantifies transcript or gene abundance in individual cells. Experiments can span 10^6 to 10^10 reads, while existing workflows can require extensive time and disk space or memory that grows with dataset size. kallisto-bustools achieves near-optimal speed, constant memory, scaling to arbitrarily large datasets, Cell Ranger-consistent downstream analyses, and fast RNA-velocity analysis.

relations.statement: This publication contains this grounded claim.

evidence.span: RNA velocity. A human reference transcriptome FASTA file of exonic transcripts and a reference genome FASTA were obtained from the University of California Santa Cruz Genome Browser, build December 2013 GRCh38. A BED file of intronic transcripts, with an L−1 (where L is the read length) flanking sequence added to each end, was also obtained from the University of California Santa Cruz Genome Browser. A unique number was appended to the end of each intronic transcript in the BED file. The genome FASTA and the intronic BED file were used with bedtools getfasta to construct an intronic FASTA file. The intronic and exonic FASTA files were combined and an index was built with kallisto index. The reads were aligned to the index using kallisto bus. The barcodes in the resultant BUS file were error corrected with bustools correct and then sorted with bustools sort. To isolate the intronic counts and exonic counts for each barcode, bustools capture was run twice: once using the list of intronic transcripts and once using the list of exonic transcripts. The spliced count matrices were made by using bustools count on the intron-captured split.bus file, and the unspliced count matrices were made by using bustools count on the exon-captured split.bus file. Both matrices were loaded into an annotated data frame in a Jupyter notebook for downstream analysis.

object.label: The same Hamming-distance-one correction can be applied to barcodes from multiple assays.
Universal preprocessing of single-cell genomics data
object.description: Large single-cell atlases depend on comparing datasets generated by many assays, so preprocessing must be consistent before biological interpretation begins. Existing workflows are often assay-specific, while read structures, barcode correction, and UMI/read counting differ across RNA, ATAC, protein, tags, and spatial modalities. cellatlas uses machine-readable seqspec files to configure modular tools for uniform preprocessing across nine datasets, modalities, and single-cell technologies.

relations.statement: This publication contains this grounded claim.

evidence.span: Sequencing machines used to sequence the libraries produced with genomics assays may generate reads with errors in barcode sequences affecting the ability for barcode-barcode registration in multi-modal assays. Preprocessing tools that perform discordant barcode error correction strategies on each modality may lose barcodes due to mismatches in correction. To address this, universal preprocessing requires consistent error correction strategies. The kallisto bustools workflow achieves a good tradeoff between speed, memory, and barcode recovery for the Hamming-1 distance barcode error correction strategy and can be consistently applied to barcodes from multiple assays (Melsted et al. 2021).

Rigorous quantitative neuron-type definitions have remained elusive because neurons are locally and projectionally heterogeneous. An integrated mouse, marmoset, and human primary-motor-cortex atlas connected molecular taxonomies with spatial, morphological, physiological, connectivity, developmental, and regulatory features while identifying a conserved hierarchical transcriptomic taxonomy.

relations.statement: DANDI archive is an author of A multimodal cell census and atlas of the mammalian primary motor cortex.

object.label: Gabriella E. Martyn
Deciphering the impact of genomic variation on function
object.description: Genomic variation can reveal mechanisms of human biology and genetic predisposition to disease. Understanding how variants alter genome function and phenotype remains challenging without a systematic catalogue of their effects. IGVF combines single-cell mapping, genomic perturbation, and predictive modeling across hundreds of cell types and states, integrating the resulting data, predictions, standards, and pipelines into an open resource.

relations.statement: Gabriella E. Martyn is an author of Deciphering the impact of genomic variation on function.

The IGVF Consortium brings together more than 120 laboratories to integrate single-cell mapping, systematic perturbation, predictive modeling, and a preliminary variant-effect map spanning gene expression, protein activity, and molecular networks.

object.label: Lior Pachter
A human commons cell atlas reveals cell type specificity for OAS1 isoforms
object.description: OAS1 isoforms have distinct antiviral activities, and protection requires expression in the infected cell type. Existing cell atlases report gene-level expression and lose isoform information. A uniformly rebuilt 2.9-million-cell, 27-tissue atlas enabled isoform quantification and identified high OAS1 p44b expression specifically in spermatogenic germ cells.

relations.statement: Lior Pachter is an author of A human commons cell atlas reveals cell type specificity for OAS1 isoforms.

object.label: A machine-readable specification for genomics assays
object.description: Understanding the structure of sequenced genomics-library fragments is essential for accurate read preprocessing. Different assays require custom preprocessing, while existing programs do not exploit shared sequence-element structure and common file formats cannot flexibly annotate complex reads. Seqspec provides a human- and machine-readable YAML specification for standardized preprocessing and can generate technology strings for kallisto bustools, simpleaf/alevin-fry, and STARsolo.

relations.statement: Lior Pachter is an author of A machine-readable specification for genomics assays.

object.label: A machine-readable specification for genomics assays
object.description: Accurate preprocessing of genomics reads depends on knowing how biological and technical sequences are arranged in each library. Assay-specific scripts, divergent parameters, absent sequence annotations, and non-machine-readable library descriptions make uniform processing, comparison, and reanalysis difficult. Seqspec provides a YAML-based library specification and command-line tool that validates assay descriptions and generates technology strings for preprocessing tools.

relations.statement: Lior Pachter is an author of A machine-readable specification for genomics assays.

object.label: A multimodal cell census and atlas of the mammalian primary motor cortex
object.description: Discovering and mapping brain cell types is necessary for understanding brain architecture, development, function, and disease. Rigorous quantitative neuron-type definitions have remained elusive because neurons are locally and projectionally heterogeneous. An integrated mouse, marmoset, and human primary-motor-cortex atlas connected molecular taxonomies with spatial, morphological, physiological, connectivity, developmental, and regulatory features while identifying a conserved hierarchical transcriptomic taxonomy.

relations.statement: Lior Pachter is an author of A multimodal cell census and atlas of the mammalian primary motor cortex.

object.label: A transcriptomic and epigenomic cell atlas of the mouse primary motor cortex
object.description: Brain circuits contain highly diverse cell types whose molecular and regulatory identities require measurements across complementary modalities. Existing single-cell assays reveal different aspects of those identities and can vary in sensitivity. Transcriptomic and epigenomic profiles from more than 500,000 mouse primary motor cortex cells resolved over 56 reproducible neuronal cell types and thousands of concordant marker genes and regulatory elements.

relations.statement: Lior Pachter is an author of A transcriptomic and epigenomic cell atlas of the mouse primary motor cortex.

object.label: Algorithms for a Commons Cell Atlas
object.description: Cell atlases organize representative datasets, cell types, and marker genes across tissues. Manual duplicated curation, inconsistent preprocessing, and a lack of compatible tools make large atlases difficult to reprocess and update. The Commons Cell Atlas supplies validated infrastructure for fast iterative processing, including modular count-matrix workflows that support human and other organism atlases.

relations.statement: Lior Pachter is an author of Algorithms for a Commons Cell Atlas.

object.label: Assessing the multimodal tradeoff
object.description: Multimodal assays can register chromatin accessibility and gene expression in the same cells, simplifying connections between the two measurements. Assessing tradeoffs across technologies requires uniform processing because distinct assay read structures complicate cross-platform comparisons. snATAK produces results concordant with Cell Ranger while running much faster, and its uniform processing identifies technology-choice tradeoffs in multimodal single-nucleus genomics.

relations.statement: Lior Pachter is an author of Assessing the multimodal tradeoff.

object.label: Author Correction: Principles of open source bioinstrumentation applied to the poseidon syringe pump system
object.description: Reliable open-instrument benchmarks depend on accurate figures. The original Poseidon Figure 4a replotted the wrong Harvard-apparatus subsets. A corrected Figure 4a and legend replace the erroneous subset in the syringe-pump comparison.

relations.statement: Lior Pachter is an author of Author Correction: Principles of open source bioinstrumentation applied to the poseidon syringe pump system.

object.label: Benchmarking of lightweight-mapping based single-cell RNA-seq pre-processing
object.description: Growing single-cell RNA-seq datasets require preprocessing tools that are both accurate and computationally efficient. Technology-specific preprocessing solutions do not scale well as datasets grow. kallisto-bustools and Salmon-Alevin-fry produced similar downstream results, but Salmon-Alevin-fry was slower, required more memory, and made large-dataset processing more expensive.

relations.statement: Lior Pachter is an author of Benchmarking of lightweight-mapping based single-cell RNA-seq pre-processing.

object.label: Characterization of spatial homogeneous regions in tissues with concordex
object.description: Spatially resolved transcriptomics enables study of gene-expression variation across tissues, but cell-type spatial distributions confound identification of spatially variable genes. Analyses therefore need to distinguish cell-type-distribution effects from cell-type-independent spatial effects. concordex identifies cell-type-homogeneous domains efficiently across platforms and tissue types, facilitating decomposition of expression into cell-type and spatial variation and revealing subtle gene-variation patterns.

relations.statement: Lior Pachter is an author of Characterization of spatial homogeneous regions in tissues with concordex.

object.label: Comparative survey-based study of noninvasive saliva collection devices
object.description: Saliva-based testing is valuable because it can make diagnostic sampling less invasive and easier to deploy at scale. The practical challenge is that swabs, funnels, and passive drool devices differ in efficiency, readability, leakage, and user burden, leaving collection protocols unstandardized. Comparing five saliva-collection devices identifies differences in collection efficiency, readability, leakage, and user burden that inform safer and easier device design.

relations.statement: Lior S. Pachter is an author of Comparative survey-based study of noninvasive saliva collection devices.

object.label: Comparative survey-based study of noninvasive saliva collection devices
object.description: Saliva is a valuable sample for noninvasive diagnosis. Collection-device usability can affect its diagnostic effectiveness. Across five swab, funnel, and passive-drool designs evaluated in 60 healthy adults, no device met every requirement for efficient, easy, safe, and leak-free collection.

relations.statement: Lior S. Pachter is an author of Comparative survey-based study of noninvasive saliva collection devices.

object.label: Deciphering the impact of genomic variation on function
object.description: Genomic variation can reveal mechanisms of human biology and genetic predisposition to disease. Understanding how variants alter genome function and phenotype remains challenging without a systematic catalogue of their effects. IGVF combines single-cell mapping, genomic perturbation, and predictive modeling across hundreds of cell types and states, integrating the resulting data, predictions, standards, and pipelines into an open resource.

relations.statement: Lior Pachter is an author of Deciphering the impact of genomic variation on function.

object.label: Decrease in ACE2 mRNA expression in aged mouse lung
object.description: ACE2 is a critical SARS-CoV-2 receptor, and age-related ACE2 expression has been proposed to affect COVID-19 susceptibility and severity. Human age-dependent ACE2 expression data are limited, so cell-type-resolved mouse lung data were used to examine age-associated ACE2 mRNA differences. Old mouse lungs show reduced ACE2 mRNA, with ciliated-cell expression and abundance shifts contributing to the decrease, while TMPRSS2 mRNA does not change significantly with age.

relations.statement: Lior Pachter is an author of Decrease in ACE2 mRNA expression in aged mouse lung.

object.label: Depth normalization for single-cell genomics count data
object.description: Single-cell genomics normalization must account for variable sequencing depth while stabilizing variance and preserving biological structure. Jointly achieving depth normalization and variance stabilization remains unresolved among widely used methods. Analysis of 526 single-cell RNA-seq datasets supports proportional fitting before log transformation followed by a second proportional fitting step.

relations.statement: Lior Pachter is an author of Depth normalization for single-cell genomics count data.

object.label: Depth normalization for single-cell genomics count data
object.description: Single-cell count normalization should stabilize variance, account for cell depth, and preserve within-cell abundance order. No existing method satisfied all three criteria on Angelidis2019, while common transforms retained depth correlation or altered within-cell ranks. PFlogPF is the only feature-relabeling-equivariant method satisfying all three criteria, and its shifted-CLR-equivalent formulation outperformed other methods across hundreds of datasets.

relations.statement: Lior Pachter is an author of Depth normalization for single-cell genomics count data.

object.label: Depth normalization for single-cell genomics count data
object.description: Single-cell count normalization should stabilize variance, account for sequencing depth, and preserve within-cell feature order. Jointly achieving variance stabilization and depth normalization remains debated, and no existing method satisfied all three desired properties in the evaluated dataset. PFlogPF is the only feature-relabeling-equivariant method satisfying all three properties and outperformed alternative normalizations across hundreds of single-cell RNA-seq datasets.

relations.statement: Lior Pachter is an author of Depth normalization for single-cell genomics count data.

object.label: Design principles for open source bioinstrumentation: the poseidon syringe pump system as an example
object.description: Rapidly changing single-cell genomics benefits from adaptable laboratory hardware, while shared open designs can keep instrument developers from starting from scratch. Open bioinstruments still need concrete design guidance to remain functional, robust, simple, modular, benchmarked, and documented. Poseidon demonstrates these principles with a customizable syringe-pump and microscope system that costs under $400, assembles in under an hour, and performs microfluidic experiments.

relations.statement: Lior Pachter is an author of Design principles for open source bioinstrumentation: the poseidon syringe pump system as an example.

object.label: Determining gene specificity from multivariate single-cell RNA sequencing data
object.description: Multivariate single-cell experiments can assay gene specificity across sex, tissue, age, genotype, and cell state. Existing specificity measures largely overlook multivariate structure or fail to decompose coherently across hierarchical partitions. Ember supplies three entropy-based metrics and is the only method shown to satisfy four desired specificity properties, revealing context-dependent markers, housekeeping genes, strain-driven cell-type switching, tissue-dominated mouse variation, and cell-type-dominated human PBMC variation.

relations.statement: Lior Pachter is an author of Determining gene specificity from multivariate single-cell RNA sequencing data.

object.label: Isoform cell-type specificity in the mouse primary motor cortex
object.description: Isoform regulation is crucial for neuronal differentiation and is implicated in neurodevelopmental and neuropsychiatric disease. Most single-cell brain studies rely on gene-level measurements, which can mask cell-type isoform shifts. Linking SMART-seq isoform resolution with 10x Genomics-defined cell types and MERFISH spatial measurements revealed extensive cell-type-specific isoform diversity in mouse primary motor cortex and refined cell types beyond gene-level estimates.

relations.statement: Lior Pachter is an author of Isoform cell-type specificity in the mouse primary motor cortex.

object.label: kallisto, bustools and kb-python for quantifying bulk, single-cell and single-nucleus RNA-seq
object.description: RNA-seq assays quantify RNA species from bulk tissue, single cells, or single nuclei. Preprocessing must map reads, handle assay-specific barcodes and UMIs, and support mature or nascent RNA quantification across assay types. kallisto, bustools, and kb-python provide free open-source workflows that produce gene-expression quantifications from raw reads for bulk, single-cell, and single-nucleus RNA-seq.

relations.statement: Lior Pachter is an author of kallisto, bustools and kb-python for quantifying bulk, single-cell and single-nucleus RNA-seq.

object.label: kallisto, bustools and kb-python for quantifying bulk, single-cell and single-nucleus RNA-seq
object.description: RNA-seq preprocessing must convert raw reads into expression measurements for bulk, single-cell, and single-nucleus assays. The workflow must coordinate reference generation, mapping, quantification, and assay-specific read structures. kb-python reduces kallisto-bustools preprocessing to kb ref and kb count while supporting bulk, single-cell, single-nucleus, and joint nascent/mature-RNA analyses.

relations.statement: Lior Pachter is an author of kallisto, bustools and kb-python for quantifying bulk, single-cell and single-nucleus RNA-seq.

object.label: Long-read sequencing transcriptome quantification with lr-kallisto
object.description: Definitive full-length isoform quantification would extend RNA measurement beyond affordable gene-level short-read counts. Long-read data properties, isoform complexity, genetic variation, and much higher error rates create bioinformatic challenges. lr-kallisto makes pseudoalignment feasible for long reads while retaining efficiency and accurately quantifying biological and simulated data across error rates.

relations.statement: Lior Pachter is an author of Long-read sequencing transcriptome quantification with lr-kallisto.

object.label: Long-read sequencing transcriptome quantification with lr-kallisto
object.description: Long-read sequencing platforms can support full-length isoform quantification, but isoform complexity, genetic variation, and long-read error profiles create computational challenges. Efficient methods are needed to accurately associate long reads with transcripts of origin across current long-read data types. lr-kallisto accurately and efficiently quantifies long-read RNA-seq libraries, supports bulk, single-cell, and single-nucleus data, benefits from exome capture, and uses less memory than compared long-read tools.

relations.statement: Lior Pachter is an author of Long-read sequencing transcriptome quantification with lr-kallisto.

object.label: Low-cost, scalable, and automated fluid sampling for fluidics applications
object.description: Automated microfluidic-stream fraction collection is preferable to tedious, error-prone manual collection. Commercial fraction collectors are often expensive and hard to customize, while existing open-source collectors can remain complex and difficult to source or manufacture. Colosseum is a low-cost, modular, one-motor automated fraction collector that can be built from off-the-shelf and 3D-printed components, assembled quickly, and used for accurate fraction collection across a wide flow-rate range.

relations.statement: Lior Pachter is an author of Low-cost, scalable, and automated fluid sampling for fluidics applications.

object.label: Markedly heterogeneous COVID-19 testing plans among US colleges and universities
object.description: US colleges inviting students back for fall 2020 needed mitigation plans to reduce SARS-CoV-2 spread and identify outbreaks rapidly. Public communications about return-to-campus plans were often opaque. Testing plans at more than 500 institutions were highly variable and muddled, ranging from regular testing of students, staff, and faculty to no testing.

relations.statement: Lior Pachter is an author of Markedly heterogeneous COVID-19 testing plans among US colleges and universities.

object.label: Massively scaled-up testing for SARS-CoV-2 RNA via next-generation sequencing of pooled and barcoded nasal and saliva samples
object.description: Asymptomatic and presymptomatic SARS-CoV-2 infectivity makes molecular screening important for pandemic control. RT-qPCR capacity, result delays, RNA extraction, and approximately US$100 test costs limited widespread regular testing. SwabSeq uses pooled next-generation sequencing with barcoded nasal or saliva samples and synthetic RNA standards to run extraction-free testing with qPCR-comparable performance, under-24-hour turnaround, and more than 80,000 returned results.

relations.statement: Lior Pachter is an author of Massively scaled-up testing for SARS-CoV-2 RNA via next-generation sequencing of pooled and barcoded nasal and saliva samples.

object.label: Metadata retrieval from sequence databases with ffq
object.description: Public sequencing data are increasingly reused alongside new experiments, making metadata collation essential for understanding samples and acquiring raw data. Existing retrieval tools cover only a limited range of databases. ffq accepts accessions or paper DOIs and returns current JSON metadata from SRA, GEO, ENA, DDBJ GEA, and ENCODE through a modular command-line interface.

relations.statement: Lior Pachter is an author of Metadata retrieval from sequence databases with ffq.

object.label: Metadata retrieval from sequence databases with ffq
object.description: Public sequencing data are increasingly reused with new experiments, making metadata collation and raw-data acquisition essential. Existing metadata tools cover a limited set of databases, while user-uploaded sequencing metadata have little standardization. Ffq exploits shared database hierarchies to retrieve accession- or DOI-associated metadata and raw-data links as JSON and can extend to genomic databases with programmatic access.

relations.statement: Lior Pachter is an author of Metadata retrieval from sequence databases with ffq.

object.label: Modular, efficient and constant-memory single-cell RNA-seq preprocessing
object.description: Single-cell RNA-seq preprocessing quantifies transcript or gene abundance in individual cells. Experiments can span 10^6 to 10^10 reads, while existing workflows can require extensive time and disk space or memory that grows with dataset size. kallisto-bustools achieves near-optimal speed, constant memory, scaling to arbitrarily large datasets, Cell Ranger-consistent downstream analyses, and fast RNA-velocity analysis.

relations.statement: Lior Pachter is an author of Modular, efficient and constant-memory single-cell RNA-seq preprocessing.

object.label: Normalization for sampled count data
object.description: Genomics count normalization should stabilize technical variance, account for depth, and preserve within-cell abundance order. Common proportional-fitting and log workflows can retain depth dependence and conflate scaling with pseudocount choice. PFlog separates pseudocount choice from centered-log-ratio geometry, uniquely satisfies the three normalization desiderata, and outperformed alternatives across hundreds of single-cell RNA-seq datasets.

relations.statement: Lior Pachter is an author of Normalization for sampled count data.

object.label: Normalization of single-cell RNA-seq counts by log (x+ 1) or log (1+ x)
object.description: Differences in ACE2 mRNA abundance were proposed to influence COVID-19 severity. ACE2 estimates from single-cell RNA-seq commonly use filtered, normalized counts, yet conditioning on nonzero counts and applying log1p distort expectations for lowly expressed genes. These choices made a reported ACE2 comparison misleading and have contributed to misleading published results.

relations.statement: Lior Pachter is an author of Normalization of single-cell RNA-seq counts by log (x+ 1) or log (1+ x).

object.label: Principles of open source bioinstrumentation applied to the poseidon syringe pump system
object.description: Open bioinstrumentation can lower costs and let laboratories adapt hardware to fast-changing biological experiments. Adoption is limited when designs are hard to build, unsafe, poorly documented, or insufficiently benchmarked. The sub-$400 Poseidon syringe pump and microscope system demonstrates functional, robust, safe, simple, modular, benchmarked, and documented open bioinstrumentation.

relations.statement: Lior Pachter is an author of Principles of open source bioinstrumentation applied to the poseidon syringe pump system.

object.label: Pseudoalignment facilitates assignment of error-prone Ultima Genomics reads
object.description: Lower sequencing costs could broaden biological and clinical projects, but new platforms must still yield assignable reads. Ultima Genomics single-cell RNA-seq reads show elevated errors in and near homopolymers and lower quality than matched Illumina reads. Pseudoalignment compensates for these errors and assigns Ultima reads better than standard read alignment.

relations.statement: Lior Pachter is an author of Pseudoalignment facilitates assignment of error-prone Ultima Genomics reads.

object.label: Quantifying orthogonal barcodes for sequence census assays
object.description: Barcode-based sequence census assays can label biological features, but barcode design and technical noise complicate quantification. Assay-specific tools can be slow, memory-intensive, and hard to standardize across multimodal, multiplexing, and perturbation assays. kITE uniformly quantifies orthogonal barcode assays with fast, memory-efficient kallisto-bustools processing, while qcbc evaluates barcode-set quality and identifies ambiguity from shared subsequences, homopolymers, and low-diversity designs.

relations.statement: Lior Pachter is an author of Quantifying orthogonal barcodes for sequence census assays.

object.label: Quantifying orthogonal barcodes for sequence census assays
object.description: Orthogonal barcodes encode biological and technical information across multimodal, multiplexing, and perturbation assays. Barcode quantification is complicated by design and technical noise, while assay-specific tools can be slow, memory-intensive, and introduce batch effects. kITE quantifies diverse barcode assays with high agreement and lower runtime and memory than comparators, while qcbc detects shared subsequences responsible for improper quantification.

relations.statement: Lior Pachter is an author of Quantifying orthogonal barcodes for sequence census assays.

object.label: Quantitative assessment of single-cell RNA-seq clustering with CONCORDEX
object.description: Single-cell RNA-seq analyses often rely on two-dimensional kNN-graph embeddings that can distort graph structure and invite visual overinterpretation. A direct quantitative method is needed to test whether categorical labels agree with local neighborhoods without depending on UMAP views. CONCORDEX quantifies label-neighborhood concordance, correlates with simulated assignment accuracy, and exposes misleading integration and clustering interpretations.

relations.statement: Lior Pachter is an author of Quantitative assessment of single-cell RNA-seq clustering with CONCORDEX.

object.label: Quantitative assessment of single-cell RNA-seq clustering with CONCORDEX
object.description: Spatial transcriptomics aims to partition tissues into functionally or compositionally homogeneous domains. Defining such regions requires relating local cell-type composition to transcriptomic or spatial neighborhood structure. concordex identifies spatial homogeneous regions efficiently and effectively across tissue types, and it can also assess concordance between clustering-derived partitions and k-nearest-neighbor graphs in non-spatial transcriptomics.

relations.statement: Lior Pachter is an author of Quantitative assessment of single-cell RNA-seq clustering with CONCORDEX.

object.label: Reliable and accurate diagnostics from highly multiplexed sequencing assays
object.description: Scalable, inexpensive, and secure SARS-CoV-2 testing is crucial for pandemic control, and highly multiplexed sequencing assays are promising alternatives to RT-qPCR tests. Their clinical use requires reliable analysis, interpretation, and computational workflows that handle sample indices, biological targets, gene counts, and infection-status classification. A kallisto-bustools workflow processes recently proposed sequencing-based diagnostic tests quickly and with low memory, validates SwabSeq analysis against an orthogonal workflow, and extends to assays with different targets and sample-index structures.

relations.statement: Lior Pachter is an author of Reliable and accurate diagnostics from highly multiplexed sequencing assays.

object.label: Science should be machine-readable
object.description: Structured scientific content can be indexed, compared, and analyzed at scales that prose-first publication makes difficult. Scientific results remain narrative, domain-specific, and hidden within article formats that do not make them explicit. OpenEval extracted 1,964,602 claims from 16,087 eLife manuscripts, and machine and human evaluations matched for 81% of co-evaluated results while the machine assessed a larger share of manuscript claims.

relations.statement: Lior Pachter is an author of Science should be machine-readable.

object.label: Systematic cell-type resolved transcriptomes of 8 tissues in 8 lab and wild-derived mouse strains capture global and local expression variation
object.description: Cell-type-resolved expression maps can connect genomic variation to complex traits and disease predisposition. Comprehensive single-cell transcriptomes across all eight Collaborative Cross founder strains and multiple tissues have remained limited. An 8-cube of 5.2 million nuclei across eight tissues and 106 cell types and states showed transcriptome variation tracking genetic divergence, with tissue-dependent and cell-type-concentrated strain effects that highlighted immune and metabolic differences.

relations.statement: Lior Pachter is an author of Systematic cell-type resolved transcriptomes of 8 tissues in 8 lab and wild-derived mouse strains capture global and local expression variation.

object.label: Systematic cell-type resolved transcriptomes of 8 tissues in 8 lab and wild-derived mouse strains capture global and local expression variation
object.description: Mapping genomic variation onto gene expression can illuminate complex traits and disease predisposition. The challenge is resolving strain effects that concentrate in specific cell types and states linked to immune and metabolic traits. The IGVF 8-cube profiled 5.2 million nuclei across eight tissues and all eight Collaborative Cross founder strains, finding that transcriptome variation tracks genetic divergence and is greatest in wild-derived strains.

object.label: The impact of genomic variation on function (IGVF) consortium

object.label: The impact of package selection and versioning on single-cell RNA-seq analysis
object.description: Standard single-cell RNA-seq workflows rely heavily on Seurat and Scanpy for filtering, dimensionality reduction, clustering, and differential expression. Although the packages are thought to implement similar steps, they produce substantially different outputs. Package differences are comparable to analyzing under 5% of reads or under 20% of cells, while version changes also produce substantial differences that are especially pronounced in differential expression.

relations.statement: Lior Pachter is an author of The impact of package selection and versioning on single-cell RNA-seq analysis.

object.label: The impact of package selection and versioning on single-cell RNA-seq analysis
object.description: Most single-cell RNA-seq analyses use Seurat or Scanpy across a multistep workflow. Package implementations and versions can silently change results and downstream interpretation. Seurat and Scanpy differed across multiple workflow stages by amounts comparable to using 5% of reads or 20% of cells, while version changes particularly altered differential-expression results.

relations.statement: Lior Pachter is an author of The impact of package selection and versioning on single-cell RNA-seq analysis.

object.label: Universal preprocessing of single-cell genomics data
object.description: Large single-cell atlases depend on comparing datasets generated by many assays, so preprocessing must be consistent before biological interpretation begins. Existing workflows are often assay-specific, while read structures, barcode correction, and UMI/read counting differ across RNA, ATAC, protein, tags, and spatial modalities. cellatlas uses machine-readable seqspec files to configure modular tools for uniform preprocessing across nine datasets, modalities, and single-cell technologies.

relations.statement: Lior Pachter is an author of Universal preprocessing of single-cell genomics data.

object.label: Voyager: exploratory single-cell genomics data analysis with geospatial statistics
object.description: Spatial organization is central to tissue function, and exploratory spatial data analysis can reveal structure in single-cell genomics data. Decades of geospatial methods have not been fully adapted to standard spatial-omics workflows. Voyager provides local, bivariate, and multivariate spatial methods through a common interface, a geometry-aware data structure, reproducible tutorials, and consistent R and Python implementations, revealing signals such as biologically relevant negative spatial autocorrelation.

relations.statement: Lior Pachter is an author of Voyager: exploratory single-cell genomics data analysis with geospatial statistics.
